title: Landform
label: Landforms
tooltip: In the context of ecosystem settings, landforms are areas of similar topographic character based on elevation range, slope, and the distribution of upland and lowland areas.

items.tooltip: Mountains support unusually rich ecological diversity because their steep often isolated terrain. Mountains support many different habitats divided by elevation ranges and the direction a slope faces.

Hills are often natural bridges between lowlands and uplands. Their varied slopes, soils, and moisture conditions create a mix of often overlapping habitats with relatively high levels of biodiversity.

Tablelands include broad plateaus, canyonlands, mesas, buttes, and sky islands. Strong contrasts between high upland surfaces and lower surrounding terrain divide habitats by limiting movement between them.
Plains are wide, relatively flat landscapes found at many elevations. They often have less ecological variety per unit of area than other landforms, but they can be extremely productive.
